title: The Coins in the Basin
notes: Reached only with the torch actually on the basin. Withdrawing before recognising the eyes leaves the basin available to inspect again. Two of the coins are not coins. Once recognised, taking them is undoing what somebody did to a face; deliberately leaving them is letting it stand. Those later decisions are terminal for the run.

regions.title: The fountain, with the light on it

lines.text: The torch finds the bottom of the fountain. Coins, a lot of them, gone green and flat under the falling water.
What happens to these wishes come tomorrow? What happens when this fountain becomes fertilizer for a new set of offices?

Buried? Does that protect a wish or tarnish one? Who keeps our wishes when we make them? This doesn't really strike you as an area where the concerns are beyond superficial. It seems to you like neither version of what this plaza could be has any effect on your tax bracket.

choices.text: Two of them are not lying flat.

lines.text: The water keeps falling over the coins.
They are domed. Marble, not metal, and cut across the front the way an iris is cut.
The falls keep going over them. They have been under this for a while.

choices.text: take them out of the water
put them back where they were

lines.text: Colder than the water. They sit in the palm like two wet pebbles and they do not look like anything at all out of the light.
Whoever did this did not throw them. They put them down.
In the wishing well the eyes stay...
Not mine. Might be somebody's wish, and this eye symbolism just seems too dramatic.
...staring at you, pleading. A screaming sclera.
